paper.title: Coordinated Behavior on Social Media in 2019 UK General Election
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2021)
paper.version: User-supplied PDF; first page identifies arXiv:2008.08370v2 [cs.SI], 1 April 2021

reader_profile.domain: computational social science and network-based coordinated-behavior analysis
reader_profile.goal: reproduce the account-to-community characterization handoff and assess transfer to CogGuard

text_evidence_sources: PyMuPDF text layer for all 12 PDF pages
direct inspection of extracted page and crop images
limitations: No supplementary appendix or official implementation was provided with the user-supplied PDF.
The paper does not report the multiscale-backbone significance parameter, threshold increment, software versions, or random seeds.
Dataset availability is treated only as a paper-stated DOI and was not independently verified in this task.

claims.claim: The framework treats coordination as graded behavioral similarity and analyzes it across a continuum rather than emitting a single coordinated/uncoordinated label.

evidence.locator: Contributions and Method overview, PDF pp.2-4
evidence.note: The authors define coordination as latent, suspicious, or remarkable similarity and describe the six-stage framework.
Community detection is repeated while the similarity threshold increases.

caveats: The coordination scale is a percentile of one filtered graph's edge-weight distribution, not an externally calibrated probability.

claims.claim: The case study reduces 1,179,659 election-discussion users to 10,782 top-1-percent retweet superspreaders, who generated 39 percent of tweets and 44.2 percent of retweets.

evidence.locator: Dataset and User similarity network, PDF pp.3-5
evidence.note: The paper reports 11,264,820 tweets, 1,179,659 users, the superspreader selection, and retained activity shares.
Collection channels and counts are shown explicitly.

caveats: This purposive high-activity sample does not represent ordinary users or the electorate.

claims.claim: The account-to-community handoff is TF-IDF co-retweet vectors, cosine user similarity, Serrano multiscale-backbone filtering, and warm-started Louvain over increasing thresholds.

evidence.locator: Method overview and Surfacing coordination, PDF pp.4-6
evidence.note: The text names each transformation and reports 276,775 edges after backbone filtering.
The iterative removal and community warm start are specified in pseudocode.
The filtered graph retains a broad edge-weight range unlike a fixed 0.9 cut.

caveats: Backbone significance, TF-IDF details, threshold increment, software, random seed, and community lineage rules are incompletely reported.

claims.claim: The unsupervised graph partition yields seven politically and topically interpretable communities, including major-party, tactical-voting, activist, and antagonist groups.

evidence.note: Network location, political-leaning colors, community labels, and hashtag clouds align descriptively.
The authors identify CON, LAB, TVT, SNP, B60, ASE, and LCH using account and hashtag context.

caveats: Political polarity comes from seeded hashtag propagation and the interpretations are post hoc, without independent annotator agreement or ground truth.

claims.claim: Different communities persist to different coordination levels, so one fixed threshold discards groups unevenly.

evidence.note: Community-size curves have different plateaux and decay shapes; the authors suggest about 0.9 for LCH and 0.55 for ASE.
Fixed thresholds 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 retain sharply different and uneven subsets; 0.9 leaves six edges.

caveats: The suggested characteristic levels are exploratory elbow judgments, not uncertainty-calibrated estimates.

claims.claim: Density, clustering, and assortativity expose distinct structural patterns across communities as coordination increases.

evidence.note: B60 rises sharply in density, clustering, and assortativity near high coordination, while several other communities show opposite trends.

caveats: The curves are descriptive, lack uncertainty intervals, and are dependent because successive subnetworks are nested.

claims.claim: Within B60 and LCH, strongly coordinated accounts emphasize more specific campaign narratives than the full communities.

evidence.locator: Figure 8, PDF p.9 and discussion on PDF p.10
evidence.note: Word-shift panels emphasize 1950s-women terms for B60 and loan-charge terms for LCH.

caveats: Only two communities are shown, thresholds come from the same exploratory analysis, and no resampling uncertainty is reported.

claims.claim: Coordination and automation are largely orthogonal in this case study.

evidence.note: Most community Botometer means and suspension rates do not move monotonically with coordination; LCH has higher Botometer scores and B60 suspensions decline.

caveats: No correlation coefficient, uncertainty interval, missing-score analysis, or causal test is reported; suspension is not a clean automation or inauthenticity label.

claims.claim: The paper states that the 2019 UK GE dataset is publicly available for research purposes and cites DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4647893.

evidence.note: The PDF says the final dataset contains 11,264,820 tweets from 1,179,659 users and is publicly available for research purposes, with a DOI footnote.

caveats: This report did not download or independently verify the dataset record; the PDF does not provide a complete execution environment.

claims.claim: This work is not supervised community-authenticity detection: it has no authenticity labels, train/test protocol, learned classifier, or community-authenticity evaluation.

evidence.note: The paper explicitly separates coordination from inauthenticity and states that successful automatic distinction was unavailable.
The authors explicitly state that the framework still does not distinguish inauthentic coordinated behavior from authentic coordination.
Bot and suspension indicators are post hoc characterization evidence, not target labels.

caveats: The framework can feed a later authenticity model, but that downstream model and its labels are outside this paper.

claims.claim: For CogGuard, the transferable unit is a provenance-rich multilevel community characterization dossier, with authenticity left unset until independent evidence is added.

evidence.note: The paper supplies the discovery-to-characterization interfaces.

evidence.locator: Introduction and Conclusions, PDF pp.1-2 and 11
evidence.note: The paper forbids equating coordination with authenticity.

caveats: CogGuard must independently validate backbone parameters, temporal stability, lineage matching, feature calibration, and authenticity labels.
